what_its_for: Benralizumab is used to help control severe asthma in adults and children 12 years and older. It works by targeting and reducing a type of white blood cell called eosinophils, which can cause swelling and irritation in your airways. It is an add-on treatment, meaning it is used along with your regular asthma inhalers — it does NOT replace them and should NOT be used to treat a sudden asthma attack.
how_to_take: Benralizumab is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection), usually in your upper arm, thigh, or belly area. Your doctor or nurse will give you the first few doses in a clinic. After training, you or a caregiver may be able to give the injection at home using the prefilled autoinjector pen. Always follow the instructions your healthcare provider gives you. Rotate injection sites and never inject into skin that is red, bruised, tender, or hard. Let the autoinjector warm up to room temperature for about 30 minutes before using it.
dosing: The usual dose is 30 mg injected under the skin once every 4 weeks for the first 3 doses, then once every 8 weeks after that. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose schedule may differ. Do not change your dose or schedule without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, give the injection as soon as you remember or contact your doctor's office to reschedule. After that, restart your regular dosing schedule (every 4 or 8 weeks from the date of the new injection). Do not double up on doses. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist for guidance.
storage: Keep benralizumab in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do NOT freeze it, and do NOT shake it. Keep it in the original carton to protect it from light. If needed, you may store it at room temperature (up to 77°F / 25°C) for a single period of up to 14 days, but then you must use it or throw it away — do not put it back in the refrigerator after it has been at room temperature. Keep out of reach of children. Dispose of used autoinjectors in an approved sharps container.
what_to_avoid: Do not use benralizumab to treat a sudden asthma attack or sudden breathing problems — it will not work fast enough. Do not stop taking your other asthma medications (such as inhaled corticosteroids) unless your doctor tells you to, even if you feel better. Avoid injecting into areas of skin that are damaged, bruised, red, or irritated. Do not share your autoinjector with anyone else.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: signs of a serious allergic reaction such as hives, rash, swelling of your face, lips, tongue or throat, dizziness, feeling faint, or trouble breathing (these can happen within hours or even days after the injection); a sudden worsening of your breathing or asthma symptoms; fever, chills, or signs of infection; any new or unusual symptoms that concern you. Tell all of your healthcare providers that you are taking benralizumab before any procedures or surgeries.
when_it_works: Benralizumab does not work immediately. Most people start to notice fewer asthma flare-ups and improved symptoms within the first few months of treatment. It may take up to 3 months or longer to feel the full benefit. It is important to keep taking it as prescribed even if you do not notice changes right away. Regular follow-up with your doctor will help track how well it is working for you.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: It is not fully known if benralizumab is safe during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding so you can discuss the risks and benefits together. Children: Benralizumab is approved for use in children 12 years and older. It has not been fully studied in children under 12. Older adults: Benralizumab can generally be used in older adults; no special dose adjustment is needed based on age alone. Allergies: Tell your doctor about all your allergies, especially if you have had a reaction to any biologic or injectable medication before.
